First, let me say that I understand your point of view. Many of our greatest Presidents only served a single term. Lincoln, T.R., Jefferson and the highly under-rated James K. Polk, were under that six year mark you suggested. They managed to achieve more in six years than any other President. In some cases they were voted out. In others shot. Only one, Polk, simply didn't want the job any more.

Two term Presidents? Aside from Washington, the majority of two term Presidents had a terrible end to their administration (FDR being an exception. He actually became a better President). Let's look at the past thirty years.

Note: I'm going to be politically neutral. Success is not based on my political views, but success as defined by the person holding office. Please no "President 'X' sucked balls" responses!

Reagan- Rocky start, but his first term was a resounding success. Despite a hostile congress, he was able to push through a revolutionary agenda, fundamentally transforming a country. He went into the 1984 election loved by the majority. One o the last Presidents who won a second term in a landslide. His second term, however, was marred by scandals and a curtailed by a resurgent Democratic party in congress.

Clinton- His first two years went very well. He tackled issues that other people wouldn't have tried. Unlike his successors, he attempted to reform health care in an open forum with input from the country as a whole. He was well liked personally, despite some of his reforms being rejected by the voters. After the mid term election, he was forced to work with congress in crafting bipartisan reforms that were, for the most part, a success. His second term saw him embroiled in a series of bad wars, and distracted by self inflicted wounds.

Bush- There's a reason why good history books are written fifty years after the fact. The wounds still feel fresh on this one, so I'm going to try to avoid the politics. At one point, a year after 9/11, Bush had a popularity rating in the high 90s. No other President since has had that level of support. His foreign policy was agreed on by almost everyone, despite their party label. His second term, of course, was as nasty as I've seen in American politics.

So it seems like a single term is a good idea, right?

Well, not really. Look, one of the reasons why Presidents do so well in their first term, beside the honeymoon period we give them, is that pressures of re-election force them to listen a little harder to what the people want. If you took away that incentive, then you run the risk of unchecked power, where the only to way to stop them is through the process of impeachment...which is a bad way to go about it.
It's not completed yet, but as of now, how would Obama factor into this?

Oh, I try not to comment on current politics. I'm too much of an armchair historian. I love reading the heated debates about tariff bills where the death of the republic was proclaimed over issues that now seem utterly nonsensical today.

If I had to make a guess, I don't see his second term ending well. That said, future generations will view him kindly. Look at JFK. Had he lived, he wouldn't be remembered as a reat President. He might have even lost to Goldwater. Instead he now represents an earlier age, and stands as a reminder of sacrifice. Here in Buffalo, there isn't a single Irish bar that doesn't have his portrait hanging in it. Obama will be the same way.
